[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Containerization (Docker) and Orchestration (Kubernetes) in Microservices"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Microservices architecture breaks down monolithic applications into smaller, independent services. However, deploying and managing dozens or hundreds of these services introduces significant operational complexity. This tutorial explores how Docker containerization and Kubernetes orchestration solve these challenges."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Containerization with Docker"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker packages an application and its dependencies into a single container image. This ensures that the service runs reliably across different environments, from a local developer laptop to a cloud-based production cluster."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /usr/src/app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["npm", "start"]"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Isolation: Each microservice runs in its own isolated user space with dedicated dependencies."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Portability: Write once, run anywhere without worrying about missing system libraries."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Orchestration with Kubernetes"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Docker handles individual containers, Kubernetes (K8s) manages clusters of containers at scale. It automates deployment, scaling, networking, and load balancing across multiple server nodes."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: user-service
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: user-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: user-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: user-service
        image: myregistry/user-service:1.0.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Auto-scaling: Automatically scale microservices up or down based on CPU utilization or custom metrics."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Self-healing: Automatically restarts failed containers, replaces unhealthy nodes, and reschedules pods."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Service Discovery and Load Balancing: Expose containers using a DNS name or their own IP address and distribute traffic evenly."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Combining Docker and Kubernetes forms the foundation of modern cloud-native microservices. Docker provides the standardized packaging, while Kubernetes delivers the robust control plane needed to orchestrate them reliably at scale."}]
